subject: TransitIQ – MSA/DPA redlines and exceptions: proposed action plan
messages:
From: Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@transitiq.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Finch <oliver.finch@transitiq.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: TransitIQ – proposed MSA/DPA redlines for integration

Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — TransitIQ is excited about the connector. Our legal team has completed an initial pass on Redwood's MSA and DPA and attached redlines for your review. High-level items we're flagging: 

- Data processing: need explicit language on purpose limitation and subprocessor notice + opt-out for specific subprocessors.
- Liability cap: TransitIQ cannot accept an unconstrained or product-of-revenue multiple; proposing a $2M cap tied to fees paid in last 12 months.
- Indemnity: ask to narrow indemnity to IP infringement only and remove broad third-party claims tied to customer data.
- Audit & security: require annual audit rights limited to SOC reports + 30 days notice; if Redwood handles logs for >90 days we need additional retention controls.
- Data residency: TransitIQ will require EU customer data to stay in EU regions for the first year.

Attached are our redlined MSA and DPA (marked). We can be flexible on some points if we map them to the SOW's responsibilities or put higher risk items into an implementation addendum.

Can you confirm timeline for: legal review, SOC 2 evidence, and a proposed SOW that captures responsibilities (who stores what and for how long)? We'd like to close commercial terms by end of next week if possible.

Attached: TransitIQ_MSA_redlines_v1.docx (redline) | TransitIQ_DPA_redlines_v1.docx (redline)

Best,
Emma Lewis
Sr. Counsel, TransitIQ
emma.lewis@transitiq.com

Emma — thanks for the redlines and clear summary. Looping in our legal (Hannah), procurement (Monica) and partnerships lead (Karthik) to triage.

Quick plan from my side:
- Hannah: please review liability/indemnity and propose acceptable cap range and any carve-ins.
- Monica: procurement to confirm whether TransitIQ PO/fees meet our standard net-45 or whether we can accept your payment proposal.
- Karthik/Me: we'll draft a short SOW that maps data flows and operational responsibilities so we can move some obligations into the SOW (logs, retention).
- Kimberly: can you pull SOC 2 link and any encryption/key management docs for Emma?

From a timelines perspective, we can commit to a 48–72 hour internal turnaround on redlines and then a consolidated response. If TransitIQ can accept a conditional EU data-residency plan (commit to region-bound routing for EU customer tenancy + 90-day migration path), that may solve the immediate blocker.

I'm CC'ing the attachments we got. We'll push an internal redline set back to you by EOD Friday.

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: TransitIQ – proposed MSA/DPA redlines for integration (internal)

Team — I reviewed TransitIQ's redlines and did a quick triage. Key notes (owner in parentheses):

1) Liability cap (owner: Hannah)
- TransitIQ's $2M ask is reasonable given anticipated first-year fees (expected < $1.2M) — recommend counteroffer: $2M sliding to 3x annual fees if there is known retention of PII across >6 months and expanded support SLAs.

2) Indemnity (owner: Hannah)
- Push to narrow to IP infringement + gross negligence. We should decline an open third-party claims indemnity tied to customer data processing — instead offer a defined carveout for properly scoped misuse.

3) Subprocessors & DPIA (owner: Kimberly / Ops)
- We can provide a subprocessors list and 30-day notice; opt-out for specific subprocessors is high friction — propose right to object and a remediation plan instead. Kimberly, can you confirm ops' ability to provide per-tenant EU routing for year one?

4) Audit rights & SOC (owner: Kimberly)
- We should give SOC2 Type II report and a standard security questionnaire; limit intrusive audits to material incidents only.

5) Data residency (owner: Monica / Ops)
- If TransitIQ requires hard-coded EU residency for their EU customers, we can support a contractual routing commitment in the SOW for up to 12 months; after that revisit. Monica, note possible commercial implications.

Action items: Hannah to produce redline suggestions for liability/indemnity by EOD Thursday; Monica to confirm PO/terms and any billing constraints; Kimberly to produce SOC2 link + a short note on per-tenant routing feasibility. I'll consolidate and we send a single consolidated redline pack to TransitIQ Friday morning.

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

From: Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@transitiq.com>

Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TransitIQ – MSA/DPA redlines and exceptions: proposed action plan

Dylan/Hannah/Team — appreciate the quick internal triage and the proposed approach. TransitIQ is okay with a conditional routing commitment in the SOW for EU tenancy provided we get written confirmation of:

- Region-bound routing for EU customers for 12 months (then review), and
- SOC2 Type II report prior to pilot start, plus encryption-at-rest details.

We can accept a liability cap tied to fees with the $2M floor (as discussed) if Redwood can commit to the routing + SOC evidence. Oliver and I will review your consolidated redlines once received Friday and push for internal approval. If everything aligns, we can sign the MSA and start SOW drafting next week.

Attached: TransitIQ_SOW_draft_v0.9.pdf (initial SOW template for comments)

Thanks — looking forward to the consolidated redline pack.

Best,
Emma Lewis
Sr. Counsel, TransitIQ
